$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.23,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.23/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and c766b6e849ce6fb8026a6e24a04e82bb25948c27ca79f0d761ea2bfbb3571f33 and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.23/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
c766b6e849ce6fb8026a6e24a04e82bb25948c27ca79f0d761ea2bfbb3571f33 is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
